title: MAPATIZYA LAWMAKER HANDS OVER TWO KEY CDF PROJECTS TO THE COMMUNITY OF MANGONDA & ZIMBA WARDS.
body_text: MAPATIZYA LAWMAKER HANDS OVER TWO KEY CDF PROJECTS TO THE COMMUNITY OF MANGONDA & ZIMBA WARDS. The Member of Parliament for Mapatizya Constituency, Emeldah Munashabantu, has commissioned key Constituency Development Fund (CDF) projects aimed at improving education, sanitation, and healthcare services in Zimba District. The commissioned projects include a 1×3 classroom block at Siameja Community School constructed at a cost of K1,265,906.80 and an ablution block with a water reticulation system at Zimba Mission Hospital Mothers’ Shelter, constructed at a total cost of K600,000 under the 2025 CDF. Speaking during the ceremonies, Hon. Munashabantu said the projects reflect the government’s commitment to taking development closer to the people and addressing pressing community needs. She noted that the classroom block will provide a conducive learning environment for pupils who previously relied on inadequate facilities such as a church building, while the health infrastructure will significantly improve sanitation, hygiene, and access to clean water for expectant mothers. Hon. Munashabantu emphasized that the lack of proper sanitation and water supply at the mothers’ shelter had long affected the dignity, health, and safety of women, adding that the newly commissioned facilities will help address these challenges. Meanwhile, Council Chairperson Loveness Chigora reaffirmed the local authority’s commitment to effective service delivery and prudent utilization of public resources. Council leadership noted that CDF continues to play a critical role in transforming communities by funding projects that directly respond to local needs. The Council also stressed the importance of promoting sanitation and hygiene, describing access to clean water and proper sanitation facilities as essential to public health and human dignity. District Commissioner has urged the community, school management, and hospital staff to take ownership of the newly commissioned infrastructure and ensure proper maintenance for long-term sustainability. title: THE CONSTRUCTION OF MARTENITY AT MAPATIZYA CLINIC IS A MILESTONE TO IMPROVED MARTERNAL HEALTH CARE-DR.MILIMO
body_text: THE CONSTRUCTION OF MARTENITY AT MAPATIZYA CLINIC IS A MILESTONE TO IMPROVED MARTERNAL HEALTH CARE-DR.MILIMO Zimba Town Council Director of Health Services, Dr. Milimo Kayawa, has described the construction of a maternity annex under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) and a mothers’ shelter by Non-Governmental Organisation On-Call Africa in Mapatizya as a significant milestone in improving maternal healthcare. Dr. Kayawa stated that the development represents a major physical transformation that government has delivered to the people of Mapatizya and surrounding areas. She explained that the new facility will allow expectant mothers to stay closer to the health centre, ensuring safer deliveries and access to proper maternal care. Dr. Kayawa further revealed that the maternity annex and mothers’ shelter will serve at least 10 rural health centres in the area, enhancing healthcare delivery across the district. She added that the maternity annex is equipped with both an antenatal clinic and a labour ward, making it easier for medical personnel to provide timely and efficient care to expectant mothers. Dr. Kayawa noted that the availability of these facilities is expected to significantly reduce cases of home deliveries, which often pose risks to both mothers and babies. Meanwhile, Government, through the CDF, has constructed the mothers’ shelter, while On-Call Africa is currently undertaking rehabilitation works at Mapatizya Clinic to further improve healthcare services in Zimba District. title: ZIMBA COUNCIL CHAIRPERSON HIGHLIGHTS STRONG PERFORMANCE IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF GOVERNMENT PROGRAMS.
body_text: ZIMBA COUNCIL CHAIRPERSON HIGHLIGHTS STRONG PERFORMANCE IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF GOVERNMENT PROGRAMS. Zimba Town Council Chairperson, Madam Loveness Chigora, says the local authority has recorded notable success in the implementation of government programmes, attributing this to unity and strong working relationships between elected officials and management. Speaking during a breakfast show on Namwianga Radio Station this morning, Ms. Chigora noted that the district has benefited from a number of development projects due to the progressive policies of the New Dawn Government. She revealed that a total of 926 pupils benefited from the Secondary School Bursaries component between 2022 and 2025, while 930 youths benefited from the Skills Development component over the same period. Additionally, 378 youth and women’s clubs received empowerment grants, and 174 individual businesses and cooperatives accessed loans under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF). Ms. Chigora further commended the dedication of council officers, stating that their commitment to service delivery has greatly contributed to the district’s achievements. She added that Zimba Town Council is among the few local authorities that fully understand and align with the vision of President Hakainde Hichilema in the effective implementation of the CDF. She emphasized that all projects undertaken by the council are community-driven and based on the needs and priorities of the people. title: ZIMBA COUNCIL URGES CONTRACTORS TO ADHERE TO PROJECT TIMELINES
body_text: ZIMBA COUNCIL URGES CONTRACTORS TO ADHERE TO PROJECT TIMELINES Zimba Council Secretary, Mr. Lubinda Mwala, has urged local contractors to strictly adhere to contracted project timelines, stating that the local authority will not entertain requests for extensions where funds have been fully disbursed and projects can be completed on time. Speaking during the opening of a contractors and suppliers sensitization meeting held in Zimba this morning, Mr. Mwala emphasized that timely completion of projects, cost-effectiveness, and quality workmanship will be key pillars in the implementation of the 2026 projects. He further called on contractors to ensure they obtain all required documentation legally and avoid compromising their bids through the use of fraudulent or illegal documents. Mr. Mwala reiterated that the local authority remains open and ready to assist citizens and stakeholders in understanding procurement and project implementation processes. He also assured contractors that preference will be given to locally based companies and suppliers in the execution of this year’s Constituency Development Fund (CDF) projects. The meeting featured presentations from the Engineering, Procurement, Legal, and Public Health departments. A total of seventeen local contractors attended the capacity-building session, including: Grerlin Building Limited, Muwemu Investment Limited, Ulonga General Dealers, Soar Construction Solutions, Ju-Gabs General Dealers, Godaso General Dealers, Omega Stationery & General Dealers, Patience Suppliers Zambia Limited, Mimak Construction & General Dealers, Zimba Youth Multipurpose, Militech Enterprise, Koyuma Suppliers, Tonacha General Dealers, Able Innovation, and Africrest Business. title: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL MONITORS CDF-SUPPORTED WATER PUMPS IN MULAMFU WARD
body_text: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL MONITORS CDF-SUPPORTED WATER PUMPS IN MULAMFU WARD Zimba Town Council, through the Department of Planning, this week took time to appreciate and monitor the works being done using the water pumps that the Government, through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), distributed to beneficiaries in Mulamfu Ward last year. A total of 20 water pumps were provided to help mitigate the effects of climate change by promoting winter farming. The pumps are enabling farmers to produce crops such as maize, vegetables, and other agricultural products, thereby enhancing food security and improving livelihoods in the community. During the monitoring exercise, officers from the Community Development Ms.Ndumwai Madabwali , Socio-Economic Planning Ms.Mainza Maambo and Public Health Mr.Thabo Sitali observed positive progress among the beneficiaries. Some cooperatives have expanded their activities and have even purchased chickens after selling vegetables produced last winter , showing the economic benefits of the initiative. Speaking during the visit, Siankope Zone WDC Zonal Chairperson, Ms. Kizito Munkombwe, said the cooperative is planning to continue with more winter farming activities shortly after the end of the rainy season. “Their target to buy more livestock in the next two years from the few produces they will make from the winter production,” Says Munkombwe. The initiative highlights the impact of the CDF programme in empowering communities and supporting sustainable agriculture in the district. title: GOVERNMENT APPROVES ELEVEN 2026 CDF PROJECTS FOR MAPATIZYA CONSTITUENCY.
body_text: GOVERNMENT APPROVES ELEVEN 2026 CDF PROJECTS FOR MAPATIZYA CONSTITUENCY. The Government has approved eleven (11) Constituency Development funded Community Projects to be implemented in Mapatizya Constituency during the 2026 period, aimed at improving access to education and health services across the constituency. In Simwatachela Ward, the education sector will benefit from the provision of desks at Kabanga Secondary School and other selected schools that enrolled Form One pupils in 2026 across the district. The health sector in Misika will see the construction of a staff house, installation of water reticulation, development of a waste management facility, and the procurement of beds, chairs, and medical equipment at Misika Rural Health Centre. In Mafumba Ward, the Government has approved the construction of a staff house, waste management system, and the procurement of beds, chairs, and medical equipment at Mafumba Rural Health Post. After many years of waiting, Chuundwe Ward will witness the commencement of construction of a Rural Health Post, bringing essential health services closer to the community. In Siamafumba Ward, a 1×3 classroom block will be constructed at Mooka Primary School, while Kanyanga Ward will benefit from the construction of a Rural Health Centre at Syejumba Village. The education infrastructure drive continues in Mangonda Ward with the construction of a 1×3 classroom block at Sindowe Primary School, and in Zimba Ward with a 1×3 classroom block at Tore Shultz Primary School. Further, Chidi Ward will benefit from a 1×3 classroom block at Simukanda Primary School, while Luyaba Ward will see the construction of another 1×3 classroom block at Kakopa Primary School. This information has been issued by the Council Secretary, Lubinda Mwala, of Zimba Town Council. Published February 26, 2026 By Mastone Moonze Categorized as Uncategorized

title: CONTRACTORS VISIT THE PROPOSED CDF SOLAR PLANT SITE IN ZIMBA DISTRICT.
body_text: CONTRACTORS VISIT THE PROPOSED CDF SOLAR PLANT SITE IN ZIMBA DISTRICT. A site visitation exercise for contractors expected to bid for the Presidential Initiatives Solar Plant to be funded using the 2026 Constituency Development Fund in Zimba District has successfully been conducted. A total of nine contractors repreesented their companies in visiting the earmarked project site as part of the pre-bid process. The proposed site is located opposite Dayow Beef Co. Limited (Abattoir). The identified land is strategically positioned within a radius of 2.3 kilometres from the ZESCO Substation, which falls well within the recommended maximum distance of 5 kilometres for efficient power connectivity. This makes the site technically suitable for the establishment of the solar power plant which will be feeding into the national grid in the district. The solar plant project is among the key measures the Government has put in place to help address the power deficit currently being experienced in the country. The project will be funded under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) and is expected to contribute to improved energy security and sustainable development in the district. Officers from Zimba Town Council who witnessed the site visitation included, Mr. Mattias Phiri – Director of Engineering,Ms. Annet Hamachili – Director of Planning,Mr. Obert Chivwanda – Senior Building Inspector and Assistant Director Mr.Sunday Nalumino. Zimba Town Council remains committed to supporting national development programmes and ensuring that projects implemented in the district meet required technical and planning standards for the benefit of the community. title: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL UNVEILS 2026 OUTPUT-BASED BUDGET ESTIMATES.
body_text: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL UNVEILS 2026 OUTPUT-BASED BUDGET ESTIMATES. Zimba Town Council held its ordinary council meeting on 30th December 2025, during which a number of key governance and development issues were discussed, including the financial outlook for the coming year. Prior to the ordinary sitting, the Council convened a special full Council meeting to consider and adopt the 2026 output-based annual budget. The budget was subsequently approved, marking an increase from K87,322,876 in 2025 to K88,945,664 in 2026. The increment has largely been attributed to increased allocations of the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) and other funding from the central government and donors. Under the approved budget, CDF has risen from K36,058,151 in 2025 to K40,032,550 in 2026. Local governance allocation has also increased from K1,641,366 to K1,797,099, while integrated development planning has been allocated K1,687,933. Economic and business development will receive K42,435. The Agriculture sector has been allocated K534,033, an increase from last year’s K459,034, while Livestock and Fisheries has received K503,176, up from K490,612. Health services recorded a significant boost, with an allocation of K6,351,370, representing a 100 percent increase from K3,200,587 in 2025. Meanwhile, social protection and community development has been allocated K17,960,467, reflecting a slight reduction from last year’s K18,193,033. Both the special and ordinary council meetings were attended by all twelve councillors and heads of departments, underscoring the importance of the deliberations. The 2026 output-based annual budget was presented by the Director of Finance, Mr. Martin Lindunda, who outlined the key changes and priorities aimed at enhancing service delivery and supporting local development in Zimba District. title: MULAMFU RURAL HEALTH POST, STAFF HOUSES AND WATER RETICULATION SYSTEM NEAR COMMISSIONING
body_text: The Mulamfu Rural Health Post maternity annex, staff houses and water reticulation system are nearing commissioning following the successful completion of key remedial works aimed at making the facility fully operational. This week, Council Secretary Mr. Collins Simoonga led a team of council officers alongside the Mapatizya Constituency Development Fund Committee (CDFC) Chairperson, Mr. Victor Sindowe, to inspect ongoing remedial works at the Mulamfu health facility. The project is being implemented with support from the Constituency Development Fund (CDF). The remedial works include the completion of plumbing installations and connection of pipes to fully operationalise the water reticulation system within the maternity annex. In addition, new solar batteries have been procured and installed to enhance solar-powered lighting, ensuring reliable energy supply for the facility. A multidisciplinary team comprising engineers, plumbers and electricians from the local authority has been stationed at the site for the past 14 days. The team is working to ensure that all outstanding works are completed to the required standards and that the facility is ready for handover to the community. Once commissioned, the Mulamfu Maternity Annex is expected to significantly reduce pressure on nearby health facilities, particularly Kabanga Rural Health Centre in Simwatachela Ward and Chidi Rural Health Centre in Chidi Ward, both of which are located approximately 15 kilometres away. The long distance has previously posed serious challenges for expectant mothers and patients seeking medical services. The completion of the facility will greatly improve access to maternal and general health services for residents of Mulamfu Ward and surrounding areas. The official commissioning date will be announced in due course. Residents of Mulamfu Ward are expected to mark the milestone as the facility begins delivering much-needed health services closer to the community.

title: PRESIDENT HICHILEMA HIGHLIGHTS GOVERNMENT COMMITMENT TO UNITY, EDUCATION AND DEVELOPMENT IN 2026.
body_text: PRESIDENT HICHILEMA HIGHLIGHTS GOVERNMENT COMMITMENT TO UNITY, EDUCATION AND DEVELOPMENT IN 2026. President Hakainde Hichilema has reaffirmed his commitment to serving the people of Zambia, stating that he intentionally chose public service because of his love for the Zambian people. Speaking during a community engagement, President Hichilema said his Government will continue taking care of citizens and called for unity and mutual care among Zambians. He cited Free Education as a key indicator of his Government’s love and commitment to the people, adding that the delivery of desks to schools under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) is another demonstration of care for communities across the country. The President further noted that the employment of teachers was a deliberate move to improve the education sector and uplift the livelihoods of citizens. He also highlighted the revival of the mining sector, saying it has brought life back to mining communities and strengthened the economy. President Hichilema added that his Government has constructed palaces for traditional leaders, built houses for chief retainers, and provided motorbikes to support traditional governance structures. Looking ahead to 2025, the President said there is a need to increase investment in the drilling of boreholes and construction of schools under the CDF, in order to further improve access to essential services. On governance reforms, President Hichilema explained that the promotion of Bill 7, now enacted as the Constitution Amendment Act No. 13 of 2025, was aimed at increasing women and youth representation in Parliament. He said the Act will promote proportional representation, thereby strengthening inclusiveness in the country’s democratic system. The President was speaking during a rally held at Choma Sports Club on Wednesday. Zimba Town Council Chairperson Madam Loveness Chigora and District Commissioner Mr. Robinson Mulamfu were among the dignitaries in attendance. title: NAKOWA MATERNITY ANNEX COMMISSIONED AND HANDED OVER TO THE COMMUNITY.
body_text: NAKOWA MATERNITY ANNEX COMMISSIONED AND HANDED OVER TO THE COMMUNITY. Nakowa residential area in Zimba Ward has received a major boost in maternal healthcare following the commissioning of the Nakowa Maternity Annex by Mapatizya Member of Parliament, Hon. Emeldah Munashabantu. Speaking during the commissioning ceremony, Hon. Munashabantu said the new facility marks an important milestone in improving access to safe and quality maternal health services for women in Nakowa and surrounding communities. She explained that the maternity annex will help decongest Zimba Mission Hospital by bringing essential maternity services closer to the people, thereby saving time, reducing costs, and ultimately saving lives. Hon. Munashabantu revealed that the facility is fully equipped with a water reticulation system and solar power, ensuring uninterrupted service delivery. She urged the community to take ownership of the facility and protect it from vandalism, emphasizing that it belongs to the people and will benefit current and future generations. She further stated that the project was made possible through the enhanced Constituency Development Fund (CDF), which she said has enabled the government to address historical development gaps in previously neglected communities. The MP assured residents of Nakowa that more development projects are still in the pipeline for the area. During her address, Hon. Munashabantu also announced that CDF funds have been allocated to improve the water supply at the mothers’ shelter at Zimba Mission Hospital. Additionally, she disclosed that funds amounting to K 800,000 have been allocated to the Southern Water Supply and Sanitation Company to extend water services to Treasure Compound as part of efforts to address long-standing water challenges. The Nakowa Maternity Annex was constructed at a cost of K1.5 million, while the accompanying water system, which will also benefit the surrounding community, cost K270,000. Hon. Munashabantu attributed the visible development in Mapatizya Constituency to responsible leadership under President Hakainde Hichilema and strong collaboration with local leadership. She called on the community to work together in safeguarding public investments to ensure they continue to improve people’s lives. The commissioning ceremony was attended by the District Commissioner, the Council Secretary was represented by Director health services, traditional leaders, senior government officials, health personnel, members of the press, and residents of Nakowa and nearby areas. title: CDF BRINGS JOY TO KAMUKKEZA VILLAGE AS 60 YEARS WITHOUT A HEALTH FACILITY COMES TO AN END.
body_text: CDF BRINGS JOY TO KAMUKKEZA VILLAGE AS 60 YEARS WITHOUT A HEALTH FACILITY COMES TO AN END. The Government has officially handed over a maternity annex in Kamukkeza Village, bringing relief to residents who for many years were forced to walk over 20 kilometres to access maternal health services. The facility was commissioned by Mapatizya Member of Parliament, Honourable Emeldah Munashabantu, and is expected to serve a population of about 6,000 people. Hon. Munashabantu described the maternity annex as a gift to the people of Kamukkeza Village, noting that the community is among the settlers who were relocated to pave way for the construction of the Kariba Dam decades ago. She said the project demonstrates the Government’s commitment to addressing historical challenges faced by marginalized communities. Meanwhile, Zimba Town Council Chairperson, Madam Loveness Chigora, urged the community to safeguard the facility against vandalism, emphasizing that it had taken many years for the area to acquire such an important health infrastructure. She further reaffirmed the Council’s commitment to delivering quality primary health services through its health department. District Commissioner Robinson Mulamfu commended Government for remembering the people of Kamukkeza Village through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF). He said CDF projects in Zimba District are being implemented in needy areas in a manner that appears almost miraculous due to their impact on people’s lives. Zimba Town Council Secretary, Mr. Collins Simoonga, also praised the community for working closely with the local authority to ensure the successful completion of the project. Several government officials, political leaders, and community members attended the commissioning ceremony, which marked the handover of the first-ever health facility in Kamukkeza Village. The maternity annex was constructed at a total cost of K2,099,616.03 under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF). Published December 24, 2025 By Mastone Moonze Categorized as Uncategorized

title: ZIMBA’S TREASURE COMPOUND SET TO BENEFIT FROM K800,000 CDF WATER PROJECT
body_text: ZIMBA’S TREASURE COMPOUND SET TO BENEFIT FROM K800,000 CDF WATER PROJECT Southern Water and Sanitation Company in Zimba district has been funded through constituency Development Fund to implement a long-awaited water supply project in Treasure Compound, an area that has experienced chronic water shortages for decades. Mapatizya Member of Parliament, Hon. Emeldah Munashabantu, today graced the ground-breaking ceremony for the project, which is scheduled to commence this month. The scope of works includes the laying and connection of water pipes, installation of a booster pump, construction of a tank stand, and erection of a 10,000-cubic-litre water tank. The pipeline will run approximately three kilometres from the main treatment plant to Treasure Compound and is expected to benefit about 8,000 residents. The project will cost K800,000 and will be implemented over a period of 60 days. As part of community involvement, Zimba Town Council has recruited 30 local residents to take part in excavation and backfilling works along the pipeline route. Speaking during the ceremony, Hon. Munashabantu described the project as a major milestone and the beginning of a lasting solution to the water challenges that Treasure Compound has faced for many years. The Member of Parliament was accompanied by CDF Chairperson Mr. Victor Sindowe, Ward Councillor Cllr. Anne Mutunda, and other community leaders. title: SIX LOCAL COMPANIES WIN CONTRACTS FOR 2025 COMMUNITY CDF PROJECTS.
body_text: SIX LOCAL COMPANIES WIN CONTRACTS FOR 2025 COMMUNITY CDF PROJECTS. Zimba Town Council yesterday held a signing ceremony for the 2025 Constituency Development Fund (CDF) projects, marking yet another milestone in the Government’s commitment to improving social infrastructure and uplifting local communities. A total of six local contractors were officially awarded contracts to undertake various community projects across the district. The awarded projects include,Construction of a 1×3 Classroom Block at Siakasipa Community School in Kanyanga Ward Contractor:Size Entreprizes,Construction of a 1×3 Classroom Block at Siameja Community School in Mangonda Ward Contractor,Lushann Powers Investment Ltd,Construction of a 1×3 Science Laboratory at Simalundu Secondary School in Siamafumba Ward Contractor, Tonacha General Dealers,Construction of a 1×3 Classroom Block at Simundivwi Secondary School in Chidi Ward Contractor,Sternab Enterprise,Construction of a Health Post at Mafumba in Mafumba Ward Contractor,Zamtrek Contractors,Construction of a Rural Health Centre at Misika Village in Simwatachela Ward Contractor,Unlimited Eagle Contractors. Speaking during the ceremony, Council Secretary Mr. Collins Simoonga commended the Government for continuing to empower local contractors through the CDF programme, saying the initiative has strengthened local economic participation and job creation. “The Local Authority will not hesitate to terminate contracts for any contractor who fails to adhere to the agreed terms and quality standards,” he warned. One of the contractors, Ms. Annie Namwala Chuulu, Director of Lushann Powers Investment Ltd, expressed gratitude to the Government for promoting gender inclusion in the construction sector. Another contractor, Mr. Thomas Chatwa, Director of Tonacha General Dealers, emphasized his company’s readiness to execute the project at Simalundu Secondary School. The commencement of works for the six projects had earlier faced delays due to administrative processes, which have since been resolved. With the signing concluded, all contractors are expected to mobilize and commence works immediately. Zimba Town Council remains committed to ensuring that all CDF projects are implemented efficiently and transparently for the benefit of the people of Zimba District. title: ZIMBA COUNCIL LAUNCHES A PLANT FIVE FRUIT TREES INITIATIVE AT HOUSEHOLD LEVEL
body_text: The Department of Agriculture services at Zimba Town Council has rolled out an ambitious “Plant a Minimum of Five Fruit Trees” initiative aimed at strengthening food, nutrition, and income security while promoting a greener environment. The programme was officially launched by the District Commissioner (DC)Mr.Robinson Mulamfu who was represented by the District Agriculture Officer (DAO) Mr.Lishomwa Mwendabai. In his keynote address, the DC underscored the importance of the initiative, noting that fruit-tree planting will enhance community resilience against the adverse effects of climate change while contributing to afforestation and reducing deforestation in the district. He further urged the local authority to mainstream the planting of at least five fruit trees in all Constituency Development Fund (CDF) projects and other construction works undertaken within the district. The DC also appealed to traditional leaders to champion the initiative by ensuring that every household under their leadership plants fruit trees. Council Chairperson Madam Loveness Chigora echoed the significance of the programme, stating that the practice of planting fruit trees is not only environmentally beneficial but also supported biblically. She said the initiative will broaden nutrition sources for the general public and create opportunities for income generation. The Council Secretary shared similar sentiments, emphasising the long-term community benefits. Representing Chief Sipatunyamana, Mr. Sindowe reaffirmed the commitment of the traditional leadership to work closely with the government and the council to ensure the initiative takes root in both Sipatunyana and Simwatachela chiefdoms. He highlighted the critical role parents play in instilling tree-planting habits in their children to secure a greener future. The initiative is expected to contribute significantly to environmental sustainability and improved livelihoods across the district as households and institutions embrace the culture of fruit-tree planting.

title: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL HOLDS FULL COUNCIL MEETING
body_text: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL HOLDS FULL COUNCIL MEETING Zimba, October 30, 2025 — Zimba Town Council today held its Full Council Meeting in the Council Chamber to deliberate on key developmental programmes and Government policy initiatives aimed at fostering sustainable growth and enhancing service delivery across the district. The meeting commenced with a moment of silence in honour of the late Mr. Ackson Sejani, former Chairperson of the Local Government Service Commission and former Member of Parliament for Mapatizya Constituency, in recognition of his distinguished and selfless service to the nation. In her address, Council Chairperson Madam Loveness Chigora urged Councillors and stakeholders to actively mobilize residents for the ongoing mass voter registration exercise, emphasizing the importance of civic participation in strengthening democracy. She further called for unity of purpose in achieving district development goals and underscored the need to expedite the implementation of Constituency Development Fund (CDF) projects while ensuring strict monitoring and accountability to prevent misuse of empowerment grants. Meanwhile, Council Secretary Mr. Collins Simoonga reported that most 2025 CDF projects are currently under procurement. He also acknowledged reports of defective boreholes in some wards and assured the meeting that corrective measures are being undertaken to ensure all works meet the required standards. Mr. Simoonga announced that the township roads have been graded to a distance of 7 kilometers, covering sections from the railway line along the T1 (Lusaka–Livingstone Road) to the Agriculture Offices, the Level Crossing to Treasure Compound, and from T1 to Muzya Stream. Works on Muzya Road have so far covered an additional 6 kilometers. He further added that the local authority completed works on the Ackson Sejani Road, linking Mapatizya Road through to Kabanga Market, covering a total distance of 87 kilometers. Providing an update on the agricultural sector, District Director of Agriculture Services Mr. Duncan Nyirongo informed the meeting that Zimba District received 8,525 input packs under the Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP), of which over 1,300 have already been redeemed. He cautioned agro-dealers against exploiting farmers and appealed to Councillors to report any cases of malpractice. The Council reaffirmed its unwavering commitment to transparency, accountability, and inclusive development, reiterating its dedication to improving the welfare and livelihoods of all residents in the district. The ordinary Council meeting was attended by His Royal Highness Chief Sipatunyana, Heads of Government Departments, Councilors, and community representatives. title: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL PRESENTS THE 2025 BUDGET
body_text: Zimba Town Council Secretary Mr. Collins Simoonga has officially presented the proposed budget estimates of revenue and expenditures for the year 2025, at the ongoing national budget hearing for local authorities. The principal officer made the budget presentation amounting to K,87,070,380 this afternoon at the Lusaka Legacy resort in Chongwe district ,where 21 local authorities are gathered for the budget hearing. The budget outlines how K 21.9 million will be channeled towards CDF Community Projects such as construction of infrastructures and grading of roads in Mapatizya Constituency 6.2 million Youth and Women Empowerment, another K 6.2 million has been allocated to both Secondary boarding School and Skills development bursaries in order to enhance quality education and reduce illiteracy levels within the district. Further, Local Governance program has received an allocation of K1.6 million, while K153,517 will be channeled towards the community engagements, the Integrated Development Planning has been allocated K1.6 million, Economic and Business Development has received an allocation of K498,222, Public Health and Environment protection will be funded a sum of K430,639. The total budget estimates for Zimba Town Council has increased by 67 percent from last year’s K 60 million due to the increased CDF allocation from K30.6 million to K36.0 million, also an increment of Devolved Function Grants from 460,328.93 to K18.7 million, an increase in the Cash For Work program and the Zambia Devolution Support Grant from World bank which has also increased from K3.7 million to K8.3 million. The ongoing National budget hearing for local authorities was held in Chongwe, Kabwe and Mpika districts from 9th to the 13th of December,2025.

title: HEALTH MINISTER IMPRESSED WITH IMPLEMENTATION OF PRESIDENTIAL DIRECTIVE ON HEALTH CARES SERVICES IN ZIMBA DISTRICT
body_text: HEALTH MINISTER IMPRESSED WITH IMPLEMENTATION OF PRESIDENTIAL DIRECTIVE ON HEALTH CARES SERVICES IN ZIMBA DISTRICT The Minister of Health Dr. Elijah Muchima, yesterday led a high powered delegation of senior government officers from the Ministry in conducting a familiarization tour of Zimba mission Hospital and Nursing school. The Minister was impressed with the implementation of the Presidential directive in constructing maternity annexes connected with running water. Dr.Muchima commended the management of Zimba mission Hospital and the Nursing school for upholding professionalism and hygiene levels at the two facilities. He acknowledged the submission by the district health department on need for more midwifery personnel to be deployed all the health facilities across the district. Dr. Muchima says the terrain and geographic set up of Zimba district deserves an ambulance to respond to numerous health care needs. The Minister says the government has procured ambulances for all the constituencies using the Constituency Development Fund,and Mapatizya is expected to receive one this year. He emphasized the need to motivate health workers through confirmations and promotions in order to enhance health care services in the Ministry. The Minister further revealed that the government is making plans to install solar power systems at all health facilities across the country in order to address power outages caused by load management. Dr.Muchima further requested civic leaders to support the health practitioners working in various rural health centres so that they deliver for the people especially that the new dawn government has put health care services as the first priority. He has since assured the nation that the government is fully stocked up to date with essential drugs to serve the citizenry. The Health Minister was accompanied with the two permanent secretaries in charge of Administration and Technical services Prof.Christopher Simoonga and Dr.Kennedy Lishimpi respectively. title: GOVERNMENT INJECTS OVER K200, 000 TO ADDRESS WATER CRISIS AT ZIMBA SECONDARY SCHOOL
body_text: Government has injected K240,000 to drill a 200-meter-deep industrial borehole at Zimba Secondary School, aimed at resolving the water crisis that threatened to disrupt the second term. The project has been financed through the 5% disaster component of the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) to address sanitation challenges at the school and create a healthy learning environment for students. According to District Commissioner and Chairperson of the Disaster Management Committee, Mr. Robson Mulamfwu, the government responded promptly to the situation after witnessing the struggles of pupils who had to walk long distances outside the school boundaries to access safe and clean water in residential areas. Mr. Mulamfwu commended the Mapatizya Constituency Development Committee for facilitating the allocation of funds to resolve the situation at the secondary school. He added that surrounding communities will also benefit from the drilled water facility, while the government continues to seek funds to drill more industrial boreholes in Treasure, Malambo, and Namadula areas. Zimba, a district in Southern Province with a low water table, has seen few industrial boreholes succeed in supplying water to households in the urban area, making this intervention crucial for the community.

title: GOVERNMENT ORIENTS MAPATIZYA COUNCILORS ON DECENTRALIZATION & PROCUREMENT PROCESSES.
body_text: GOVERNMENT ORIENTS MAPATIZYA COUNCILORS ON DECENTRALIZATION & PROCUREMENT PROCESSES. Government through Zimba Town Council has successfully conducted orientation training for all the 12 ward councilors in Mapatizya constituency with an objective of equipping them with knowledge on the implementation of the decentralization policy. The exercise which is held in the Council Chambers is aimed at making trainees understand the importance of decentralization policy in serving the people in their wards. In his opening remarks, Provincial Local Government Officer ,Mr.Charleston Hamulyata reminded councilors that the constitution recognize them as key components in delivering development through a decentralized system of governance. He explains that effective actualization of the policy, requires a clear definition of roles and relationships of institutions involved to avoid duplication and conflict. Mr.Mr.Hamulyata says decentralization is a program that involves changes in power relationship between central and local levels of government. The Provincial Local Government Officers-PLGO says a Successfull implementation of the decentralization policy is dependent on political will from councilors and other politicians in order for the citizens to embrace and understand the devolved power , responsibility and resources. Mr.Hamulyata emphasized that government demands a serious and honest approach in implementing Constituency Development Funded Projects in all wards based on the people’s needs. The training is also being attended by the Council Chairperson Ms.Loveness Chigora, Council Secretary Mr.Christopher Siasinyanga , Heads of Departments and other members of staff. title: SCHOOLS FROM FIVE WARDS EMPOWERED WITH SANITATION FACILITIES IN MAPATIZYA CONSTITUENCY
body_text: Environment Africa Zambia has dedicated today’s commemoration of International Day of Children’s in launching the installation of boreholes, bathing shelters for girl-children and VIP Toilets in Zimba District. Environment Africa WASH officer Mr. Haggai Mendai says the sanitary facilities that the organization is putting up in Zimba symbolize its commitment to creating a child-friendly community that values the rights and well-being of the young people. The Organization has been working in five wards of Zimba district namely Mbwiko, Chalimongela, Simwatachela, Luyaba and Mangonda with special attention to improving Agriculture, sanitation, environment protection, children’s rights and climate change. Zimba District Commissioner Mr. Robson Mulamfwu graced the occasion and emphasized the need to protect the rights of children as government has placed great importance on the walfare of the young people in the district. He further spelt out the government’s commitment to protecting children’s rights through the implementation of various policies such as the introduction of free education, distribution of desks and the construction of classroom blocks under the Constituency Development Fund-CDF. In a speech read on her behalf by Mapatizya Primary School Headteacher Mr. Orbit Munanku, Zimba District Education Board Secretary Ms. Inonge Rita says today’s commemoration of children’s rights should act as a wake up call for the country to serious consider the rights of the young people. She said pupils and the entire Mapatizya Primary School and community were having difficulties in accessing clean water, but the coming of the water system funded by the Environment Africa will help improve sanitation at the school. Zimba District today joined the rest of the world in commemorating the international day of children rights commemorated under the theme ” RENEWING OUR PROMISE FOR CHILDREN’S RIGHTS where all Heads of government Departments,Zimba Town Council, Traditional leaders and other stakeholders gathered at Mapatizya Primary School to commemorate the day. title: GOVERNMENT LAUNCH THE DISTRIBUTION OF CDF DESKS, AWARDING OF OVER 5 MILLION KWACHA WORTH OF GRANTS AND LOANS IN MAPATIZYA CONSTITUENCY.
body_text: Government through Zimba Town Council has launched the distribution of 2, 620 desks procured under the 2022 and part of the 2023 allocation of the Constituency Development Fund – CDF to all the schools in Mapatizya Constituency. The ceremony which was held in Kabanga area today, also saw 92 Clubs, Coorperatives and individual companies benefitting from grants and loans respectively. Mapatizya Member of Parliament Emelda Munashabantu, says the distribution of 2, 620 desks procured at K 2, 887,051 is a direct response to the increasing number of pupils that was necessitated by the coming back to school of more children due to the implementation of the free education policy. The lawmaker further advised the beneficiaries of grants and loans to prudently use the funds and venture into profitable businesses that can improve their lives and also the communities that they belong to. And Zimba Council Chairperson Madam Loveness Chigora, says the distribution of desks to the schools will undoubtedly enhance the quality education and improve the learning environment for young learners in the district. The Council Chairperson emphasized that the giving out of CDF loans and grants to the citizens is a new dawn Government’s vision to create an enabling business environment for entrepreneurship, skills development and economic growth. Meanwhile, Zimba District Commissioner Mr. Rabson Mulamfwu, says the distribution of desks is a positive response to President Hakainde Hichilema’s directive of not seeing any pupil sitting on the floor in class by the end of the year 2024. Mr. Mulamfwu has advised the beneficiaries of loans and grants to undertake the businesses and help government realise it’s vision of having an economically stable nation. A total of K2, 93, 400 was disbursed as loans to 26 cooperatives and individual companies while K 2, 143, 990 grant was awarded to 65 Women and Youth Clubs. The empowerment of grants and loans was derived from the 2023 allocation of CDF, while the procurement of desks is a combination of 2022 and 2023 funding.
